answer: Deposits are visible in thread, and nectar reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 164 aliases, and each one needs its own funded walnut account. A bond of 41% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. That bill is paid per identity, so 333 aliases cost 260 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
